- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.20) mid-horizon, model frequently underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline > 2%, model often fails to correct — add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility in early days (days 1–7) — reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.30 → +0.20 → -0.30), model often misreads momentum — apply 1–2% downward bias in forecast 10–15 days ahead.
